Calibration Table of a Fitted Survival Model

Source: R/predict_calibration.R
calibration_from_model.Rd

Validates a fitted [coxnet()], [cv_coxnet()], [joint_model()], [cox_time_varying()] or [fine_gray()] model at one horizon: the event risk is predicted with [predict_event_risk()] and passed, with the right-censored outcome from `new_data`, to [calibration_table()]. See there for the bins, the observed risks and the metrics; competing events are treated as censoring, as in [calibration_table()]. For a [fine_gray()] fit the risk is the cumulative incidence of the cause of interest and the outcome is dichotomised to that cause (`event_col == failcode`); other causes count as censoring.

Usage

calibration_from_model(
  object,
  new_data,
  time_col,
  event_col,
  horizon,
  penalty = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

object

A fitted `coxnet_model`, `cv_coxnet`, `joint_model`, `cox_time_varying` or `fine_gray_model` object.

new_data

A data frame with the predictors and the `time_col` / `event_col` outcome columns. For a `fine_gray_model` fit, `event_col` holds the competing-risk event codes (censoring code, then one code per cause), as in [fine_gray()].

time_col, event_col

Outcome columns in `new_data`: follow-up time and the 0/1 event indicator (or, for a `fine_gray_model` fit, the event codes).

horizon

A single finite, positive time: the horizon the calibration applies to.

penalty

Passed to [predict_event_risk()]; ignored for `joint_model`, `cox_time_varying` and `fine_gray_model`.

...

Passed to [calibration_table()] (for example `bins` or `conf_level`).

Value

As [calibration_table()]: a tibble with one row per model and bin, with `attr(x, "metrics")` and `attr(x, "horizon")`. For Surv outcomes the metrics are `NA` (see Details).

Details

**No summary metrics for Surv outcomes.** `attr(x, "metrics")` is always `NA` for `intercept`, `slope` and `brier` here: [calibration_table()] computes those only for a binary outcome, and no IPCW-based summary metrics for right-censored outcomes are implemented. The bins table itself (mean predicted vs Kaplan-Meier observed risk per bin) is the calibration assessment. To estimate a calibration slope yourself, dichotomise the outcome at the horizon — 1 for an event by `horizon`, 0 for follow-up past `horizon` (subjects censored before `horizon` have unknown status and are dropped) — and regress that indicator on the logit of the predicted risk, for example `glm(y_horizon ~ qlogis(risk), family = binomial())`: the coefficient of `qlogis(risk)` is the slope, and the intercept of `glm(y_horizon ~ 1 + offset(qlogis(risk)), family = binomial())` is calibration-in-the-large.

See also

[decision_curve_from_model()], [predict_event_risk()], [calibration_table()]

Examples

set.seed(1)
n <- 120
d <- data.frame(time = rexp(n, 0.05), status = rbinom(n, 1, 0.6),
                age = rnorm(n, 60, 10), sex = rbinom(n, 1, 0.5))
fit <- coxnet(survival::Surv(time, status) ~ age + sex, data = d, penalty = 0.1)
#> TempleCBE: Pinned Cox tie-handling to 'breslow' (option 'templecbe.cox_ties').
calibration_from_model(fit, d, "time", "status", horizon = 10, bins = 5)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 7
#>   model   bin     n mean_pred observed conf_low conf_high
#>   <chr> <int> <int>     <dbl>    <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl>
#> 1 model     1   120     0.215    0.216    0.150     0.305
